package_info.why_malicious: The Orion software update mechanism was compromised to deliver the Sunburst backdoor to customers. Attackers inserted a sophisticated, obfuscated backdoor into a legitimate update, enabling covert remote access, command execution, and data exfiltration from customer systems, including those in government and private sector networks. This supply chain attack facilitated widespread espionage and persistent unauthorized access.

execution_context.trigger: import-time (on service start or update installation)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Implements a covert backdoor that, upon Orion service start or update installation, establishes outbound connections to attacker-controlled servers, beacons system information, and awaits remote commands. Upon receiving commands, it can execute arbitrary code, perform lateral movement, and exfiltrate data. The code is heavily obfuscated and designed to evade static and behavioral detection.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code initiates outbound connections to external domains not associated with SolarWinds, transmits system reconnaissance data, and executes remote commands received from attacker infrastructure. Its presence in a business logic DLL, combined with advanced obfuscation and anti-analysis techniques, is highly anomalous for legitimate software.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate update code should not contain hidden remote access or command execution logic, nor should it communicate with unknown or untrusted external servers. Business logic DLLs are not expected to perform network beaconing or execute arbitrary code from remote sources.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Remote management or telemetry tools may connect to trusted vendor servers for updates or diagnostics, but such behavior is transparent, well-documented, and never obfuscated or hidden within unrelated DLLs.
key_indicators: Outbound network connections to non-SolarWinds domains (e.g., avsvmcloud.com)
Dynamic loading and execution of commands received from remote servers
Execution triggered at service start or during update installation
Presence of anti-analysis and evasion logic (e.g., delayed execution, environment checks)

attack_chain.action: Attacker compromises SolarWinds build environment and injects the Sunburst backdoor into the Orion update DLL.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious code is cryptographically signed and distributed to customers via the legitimate SolarWinds update mechanism.

attack_chain.action: Customers install the compromised update, loading the malicious SolarWinds.Orion.Core.BusinessLayer.dll into Orion services.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious code is executed on customer systems with the privileges of the Orion service.

attack_chain.action: The Sunburst backdoor beacons to attacker-controlled servers, transmits system information, and awaits further instructions.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker gains persistent, covert access to victim networks, enabling lateral movement, data exfiltration, and further compromise.

behavioral_signatures: Unexpected outbound network connections from Orion services to non-SolarWinds domains (e.g., avsvmcloud.com)
Obfuscated or anomalous code present in SolarWinds.Orion.Core.BusinessLayer.dll
DLLs or binaries exhibiting unexpected export functions or initiating network activity
Orion service processes performing network beaconing at service start or update installation
Presence of anti-analysis techniques (e.g., delayed execution, environment checks) in business logic DLLs
file_indicators: SolarWinds.Orion.Core.BusinessLayer.dll with hash not matching official SolarWinds release
Presence of unknown or modified DLLs in the Orion installation directory
Digital signatures on DLLs that do not match official SolarWinds certificates
network_indicators: Connections to known Sunburst C2 domains (e.g., avsvmcloud.com, digitalcollege.org, freescanonline.com, deftsecurity.com, thedoccloud.com, websitetheme.com, highdatabase.com, incomeupdate.com, databasegalore.com, panhardware.com, zupertech.com, virtualdataserver.com, liberomail.com, solartrackingsystem.net, webcodez.com, seobundlekit.com, virtualwebdata.com, globalnetworkissues.com, kubecloud.com, lcomputers.com, websolartech.com, solartrackingsystem.net)
Beaconing patterns from Orion servers to external IPs/domains at regular intervals
Unusual DNS queries or HTTP/S traffic originating from Orion service processes
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor Orion service processes for unexpected outbound network connections, especially to domains not owned by SolarWinds or listed as known Sunburst C2 infrastructure. Validate file hashes and digital signatures of Orion DLLs against official SolarWinds releases to detect tampering. Analyze business logic DLLs for obfuscated code, anti-analysis techniques, or unexpected export functions. Use network monitoring to identify beaconing behavior, block known C2 domains, and alert on suspicious DNS or HTTP/S requests from Orion-related processes. Correlate these indicators to distinguish malicious activity from legitimate Orion operations.
